title: Degrees of Freedom Counter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robot Arm Anatomy
description: Use the counting rule on eight mechanisms, from a door hinge to the reBot-DevArm: read the joints each one contains and work out its degrees of freedom. Used in Chapter 2.

educational.topic: Degrees of freedom and the counting rule
learningObjectives: Calculate the degrees of freedom of eight mechanisms by counting their independent single-axis joints, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Practice one rule on new cases with every joint listed, so a wrong answer shows a wrong rule and not a hidden assumption; the cases build from one joint up to the two real arms
keyQuestions: Does a prismatic joint count the same as a revolute joint?
Why is the SO-ARM101 called a 5 DOF arm in some places and a 6 DOF arm in others?
What does the 6+1 in the reBot-DevArm description mean?
commonMisconceptions: The DOF of a robot is the number of its links
Prismatic joints do not count as degrees of freedom
assessmentOpportunities: Eight committed whole-number answers, one attempt each; 7 of 8 for mastery

controls.label: Degrees of freedom
controls.range: 1 to 8, step 1, nothing chosen at the start

controls.label: Check / Next mechanism / See score / Try again
